arguments.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the ACTUAL lair scene. Image 2 is selected graphic-novel character rendering only. Images 3 and 4 are selected fog-wet-stone environment style only. Image 5 is an ORIGINAL coordinate zone guide, not final art or a strict mask. Edit the actual source locally; do not redraw this whole scene.

MOMENT: the huge hydra has just raised three heads; two undead stand inside the threshold. Preserve the current creature, guards, stone and location exactly. Give the TWO HUMANS a readable but restrained reaction to this reveal, then locally simplify the courtyard surfaces.

M AT LEFT: his eyes ALREADY point toward the hydra. KEEP that direction. In the same recognizable adult face, tighten the lower brow and jaw, tuck the chin a little, draw his shoulders into a compact protective guard, and introduce a slight rearward weight shift through the current bent knees/hips. Same planted boots and physical supports, no new step. His mouth stays controlled, no scream. Preserve exact scarf/quilting/seams, shield on anatomical LEFT forearm, EMPTY scabbard at LEFT hip, single sword in RIGHT grip with the same blade/guard/pommel and low point safely away from his feet. The shield and weapon may follow a very small natural shoulder adjustment but retain all contacts and kit sides. Not a theatrical attack or stumble.

ZOYA AT RIGHT: lift her chin/attention slightly toward the towering heads and give her an arrested breath through a tense brow, alert eyes and a subtle part in the lips, with shoulders visibly bracing. Keep her SAME adult identity, white hair streak, braid, blue cloth sleeves, brown LEATHER apron/seams and both current grounded leg supports. Her RIGHT palm remains firmly on the TOP face of the SAME irregular low block; her LEFT palm stays on its separate SIDE edge, each with its own continuous forearm and natural fingers. Only tiny head/shoulder/neck posture changes, no released hand or moved block. Same two unused wedges in the single pocket, ONE iron prybar lying outside right of stone with same bent flattened foot.

COURTYARD WATER AND FOREGROUND PAVING, indicated by slate/teal in image 5: perform an OPAQUE REGIONAL PAINTOVER replacing the mirror-like reflection stripes and many uniform tiny surface marks with TWO OR THREE LARGE CALM MATTE SLATE WASH PLANES. A few soft broken broad reflections suggest wetness; do not keep a smooth precise mirror image of every head/leg. Quiet broad stone planes and a few selective structural joints replace decorative flecks and repetitive sharp paving grain. Match the restrained value/material hierarchy of images 2–4. Keep the SAME water level, actual paving edges, boot/creature contacts and perspective. Do not blur/darken the whole frame. No new ground structures or pits. Protect the physical dull bronze threshold and its necessary soft BLUE sheen; original RIGHT gap stays unlit.

PROTECT EVERYTHING ELSE: exact original hydra THREE heads/ONE dark segmented body/FOUR actual legs and same scale, posture, crest design and tail; D1 exact existing plated/helmet armor versus D2 ragged grey-haired identity, two spears and their own arms. No new beast anatomy or replacement creature. ONE intact raised slab/guides, overhead chain/pulley/right winch/right steps, left roots/tree, far arches, same camera/crop/horizon and grey daylight. Keep current cast count, materials, wear and low cause-linked wetness. No new pose for guards/beast, new wounds, extra tools or creature, glossy skin, scream, text, border, guide marks or UI. Return the finished opaque full illustration only, same 1672x941 framing. This is one bounded acting/surface correction, not a fresh scene.
